claims.text: A partially recrystallized heterogeneous grain structure can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in an MPEA.
The CrCoNi alloy used as an example can be a single-phase FCC alloy.
The cold-rolled starting material has a high dislocation density.
The cold-rolled starting material has a uniform ultrafine-grained or nanocrystalline microstructure.
Homogeneous ultrafine-grained FCC MPEAs typically have low ductility because deformation twinning is suppressed and strain-hardening capacity is limited.
Partial recrystallization at 873 K for 1 hour followed by water quenching can produce the proposed heterogeneous structure in CrCoNi.
The resulting heterogeneous structure contains nanometer-, ultrafine-, and micrometer-scale grain populations.
Plastic-strain mismatch between soft coarse grains and hard nanograins generates significant back stress during deformation.
Coarse grains facilitate deformation twinning relative to ultrafine grains.
Twinning activates in coarse grains at lower resolved shear stress than in ultrafine-grained counterparts.
Back-stress hardening accounts for more than 80% of the stress elevation.
Deformation twinning has a delayed onset in coarse-grained regions of the heterogeneous structure.
The heterogeneous structure prevents early shear-band localization by distributing plastic strain.
Twinning-induced plasticity in coarse grains sustains strain hardening.
The heterogeneous CrCoNi alloy is expected to achieve approximately 1150 MPa yield strength and 22% uniform tensile elongation at room temperature.
A homogeneous ultrafine-grained counterpart typically exhibits less than 2% uniform elongation at a similar strength level.
A higher-temperature or longer anneal can provide a fully recrystallized homogeneous ultrafine-grained control from the same alloy.
The strategy requires stacking-fault energy low enough for twinning but high enough to avoid spontaneous martensitic transformation.
The strategy may fail in high-stacking-fault-energy alloys because twinning is suppressed.
A strain-hardening-rate upturn between 4% and 8% strain is indicative of back-stress hardening.
